In summary, our research is concerned with
the physics of high-energy proton-(proton) colliders.
the study of the behaviour of soft scattering processes at high energy, and with the calculation of the rates for exclusive processes at high energy.
the study of the high-energy limit of QCD, and the application of this to the study of the LHC physics program.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the high-energy behaviour of soft processes, and the survival of exclusive processes, are both well understood.
, although there is a lot that we do not yet fully understand about soft scattering at the LHC, the situation is not as bleak as it might appear at first glance.
, while we have a good qualitative picture, we do not have a complete quantitative understanding of high-energy soft physics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the `soft' physics of high-energy proton-(proton) colliders is well understood, and that the `exclusive' physics is also under control.

, in the absence of a theory of strong interactions at high energies, we have developed a phenomenological approach which is capable of making accurate predictions of the behaviour of a wide class of high-energy processes at the LHC.
, at the LHC, we may expect to observe the production of heavy systems (Higgs, dijets, W, Z, top, etc.) in exclusive final states at rates comparable to those in the inclusive case.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the high energy regime, the survival probability of rapidity gaps is not unity, and that, in fact, the rate of exclusive production of heavy systems is significantly enhanced.
the LHC will be an excellent machine for the study of soft and exclusive processes.
, at the LHC, one may be able to observe exclusive Higgs boson production, provided that the Higgs boson mass is less than 140 GeV.
